note: Candidate-zone screen; thermal.loops.warm.area and cold.area stay OPEN (Q38). Every value is DIAGNOSTIC; the zones are PROTOTYPE.

defense_routing.rule: hot drive blades are not the direct sink; do not spend the diagnostic root margin

study.rationale: Q38 screen: candidate warm (casing, collar, shadow panels) and cold (ring surfaces) zones against the 1800 K blade faces, to show where a gray surface rejects heat and where it absorbs more than it emits. It selects no warm or cold area.

assumptions: thin blade planes, both faces emitting, spar and truss ignored
root band treated as hot (temperature map OPEN)
gray surfaces, alpha = emissivity (owner illustration emissivity)
non-hot blockers (hull, rings, shield) exchange net zero with the receiver
open rotor bay filled at the hull radius_at; shield modelled as an aft-most disc
panels are receivers only, not blockers
ring results are averaged over azimuth (rotation average); spokes ignored
BLADES_NOT_RADIATING bounds the case only under the stated blade assumption (dark blades adiabatic); it is not a strict best case, and real COAST hot-loop duty is OPEN (Q41)
the zero-exchange assumption errs in a known direction per loop and case (zero_exchange_assumption); classes that depend on it are flagged

zero_exchange_assumption.statement: Non-hot blockers (hull, casing, rings, shield) and dark blades exchange net zero with the receiver. DIAGNOSTIC: the direction of the error is stated, not simulated.

cold.HIGH_POWER: OPTIMISTIC: the hull/casing is a >=450 K warm surface (and HP-heated) under the study's own premise, not a 320 K neighbour, so zero exchange overstates ring capacity; q_if_blockers_at_warm_W_m2 bounds it
cold.BLADES_NOT_RADIATING: OPTIMISTIC: same, the warm hull/casing seen by the rings would reduce or reverse ring capacity (q_if_blockers_at_warm_W_m2); dark blades can act either way (sink or source) depending on their temperature, and blade duty outside burns is OPEN (Q41)

warm.HIGH_POWER: NEUTRAL TO PESSIMISTIC: the casing, collar and panels are net-heated by the blades regardless; hot-neighbour blockers are already hot-class
warm.BLADES_NOT_RADIATING: PESSIMISTIC: dark blades treated as adiabatic; if colder than the receiver they are sinks, which would add capacity (reviewer estimate about +2.6 MW at the casing, enough to erase the 1.15 MW shortfall; not simulated here)

findings.assumption_direction: NEUTRAL TO PESSIMISTIC: the casing, collar and panels are net-heated by the blades regardless; hot-neighbour blockers are already hot-class

assumption_direction.HIGH_POWER: OPTIMISTIC: the hull/casing is a >=450 K warm surface (and HP-heated) under the study's own premise, not a 320 K neighbour, so zero exchange overstates ring capacity; q_if_blockers_at_warm_W_m2 bounds it
assumption_direction.BLADES_NOT_RADIATING: OPTIMISTIC: same, the warm hull/casing seen by the rings would reduce or reverse ring capacity (q_if_blockers_at_warm_W_m2); dark blades can act either way (sink or source) depending on their temperature, and blade duty outside burns is OPEN (Q41)

findings.label: DIAGNOSTIC pessimistic extreme, not a simulation: the whole blocked fraction (incl. the shield) at 450 K, and it omits the receiver's own emission toward the blocked fraction. The reviewer estimate of about 76 kW for the fore faces is HIGH_POWER with only the hull at 450 K and the shield excluded
findings.note: the actual cold load is OPEN; only the 100 kW illustration exists (40!F62)
